text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2% today to $133.43, extending a sharp decline from last week's high of $140.52. The sell-off appears tied to two converging headwinds: first, a broad unwinding of the refinery-related trade that has driven energy stocks higher this year—analysts are signaling the "boom is over" and looking elsewhere; second, the collapse of climate negotiations at COP31, which rejected a fossil-fuel-inclusive deal and may signal tougher regulatory or investor sentiment ahead for oil majors.

The timing matters: oil prices remain solid (US crude at $89.53/barrel, global at $92.94), so the stock decline isn't a commodity crash. Instead, it reflects a rotation away from the energy sector trade itself and growing climate-policy headwinds that could weigh on long-term investor appetite for large oil companies, even if near-term cash flows stay healthy.
